subject: Renewal: multi-year prepay with staged ramp — proposal attached
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Raghav <aisha.raghav@zenhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@zenhealth.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion — multi-year prepay option to cap 2027 pricing

Hi Aisha,

Hope you had a good Thanksgiving week. Our team has reviewed ZenHealth's usage patterns and the upcoming model-cost pressure for 2027. To give you pricing predictability and avoid exposure to index-based increases next year, I'd like to propose a multi-year prepay structure that locks per-unit pricing while allowing you to ramp consumption across the term.

High-level proposal (details attached):
- 3-year prepay (annual invoicing) for committed $ total of $1.2M (annual slices: $300k / $400k / $500k)
- Effective unit discount vs list: year1 18%, year2 22%, year3 28% (reflects ramp and long-term lock)
- Rolling ramp: unused prepay in any year may be applied to subsequent year up to 20% of that year’s commitment
- SLA credits and priority capacity included for Dedicated tier during business hours

I've attached a term sheet and the usage run-rate we modeled. If this structure looks promising, can we schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through the numbers and procurement timing?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: ZenHealth_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet, pricing table)
Attachment: zenhealth_usage_runrate_Q42026.csv (anonymized month-by-month run rate)

From: Aisha Raghav <aisha.raghav@zenhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — multi-year prepay option to cap 2027 pricing

Vanessa —

Thanks for this. The team likes the idea of locking pricing but a couple of flags from procurement / finance:
1) We need flexibility in year 1 — usage is still uncertain while pilot expands. Can we reduce year1 minimum to $200k and shift to heavier prepay in year3?
2) The 28% discount in year3 looks aggressive; finance will want clarity on how that maps to committed throughput and whether we can get a modest ramp credit if we hit higher-than-expected usage.
3) Any chance of a 60-day termination clause tied to regulatory change?

Can you also confirm how overage billing works if we exceed the annual prepay in a given year — will overage be billed at the locked rate or at list?

Best,
Aisha
Director, Cloud Platform — ZenHealth

Team — forwarding Aisha's notes. Key asks from ZenHealth:
- Move year1 minimum from $300k to $200k, shift volume to year3
- Clarify overage billing at locked rate vs list
- 60-day regulatory termination clause request

My suggested counter (to present if you sign off):
- Keep total 3-year commit at $1.2M but reallocate annual slices to $200k / $350k / $650k (this gives them lower year1 cash outlay while preserving overall commitment)
- Overage billed at the locked per-unit rate for the remainder of the term once they exceed annual slice; any sustained >20% overage for two consecutive quarters triggers a usage rebaseline conversation (protects us from sustained underpricing)
- 60-day regulatory termination limited to material regulatory change that makes delivery impossible; include pro-rated refund language for unused prepay if termination invoked
- Adjusted discounts: year1 15%, year2 20%, year3 25% (a bit lower than their ask but keeps margin)

Attached is a redline-ready term sheet I plan to send if you approve. Quick please — they asked for an updated proposal this week.

Thanks,
Vanessa

Vanessa / Priyom —

Thanks for the summary. High level OK but two asks from pricing:
1) Move the overall $1.2M commit to $1.25M to cover potential kernel-optimization uplift and to keep effective margin stable; we can still keep their requested $200k start. This gives us ~4% buffer.
2) Keep overage at locked rate but add a tiered overage premium beyond +50% quarter-over-quarter to protect supply during extreme spikes (e.g., +50% -> 10% surcharge, +100% -> 25% surcharge).

If both accepted, approved to present. Priyom — please update the term sheet and the revenue forecast for the quarter so I can sign off.

Marcus
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the candid feedback. Based on internal approvals, here's the updated offer we can put on the table today:
- 3-year prepay, total commit $1.25M, annual slices: $200k (Y1) / $350k (Y2) / $700k (Y3)
- Discounts: Year1 16% / Year2 20% / Year3 26% off list pricing

- Unused prepay may be rolled forward up to 20% into the next year; sustained >20% overage triggers usage rebaseline conversation
